project.one_line: A protocol-native collaboration environment where groups persist across apps, conversations modify shared state, and temporary constrained interfaces appear around the work people are actually doing.
project.core_thesis: The app should not be the permanent container. The group, its identity and its shared state persist; threads are places where people collaborate; and interfaces are temporary checkouts of the state needed for the situation.

original_thoughts.idea: ATProto as a model for application-independent data
original_thoughts.thought: The canonical data should not belong to one application. Apps should be replaceable representations over portable typed records.

original_thoughts.idea: The UI representation is a checkout
original_thoughts.thought: The UI should never be treated as the canonical state. What the user sees and manipulates is a virtualized checkout of the underlying shared state.

original_thoughts.idea: Delta.dev, but for human collaboration rather than programming
original_thoughts.thought: Take the Delta.dev collaboration model of threads, shared state, checkouts, tools and agents, but remove the assumption that the underlying shared object is source code.

original_thoughts.idea: Social media, but not bad social media
original_thoughts.thought: People gather, talk, explore, make things and act together. The goal is not publishing, engagement or attention. The social object is collaborative activity.
The LLM is not the centre of the product and does not replace the humans. People collaborate with one another while AI can research, synthesize, remember, transform and operate tools around them.
The interface may change with the work, but should not be arbitrarily generated by an LLM. It should be assembled from trusted interaction primitives and grammars.

borrowed_ideas: data that is not owned by one application
inspirations.creative_extension: Move from portable data across applications toward persistent collectives whose working interfaces can also be temporary.

borrowed_ideas: a group exists independently of any one application
membership that can be reused across spaces
governance and group norms that travel with the group
the same community can appear in different application contexts
inspirations.creative_extension: Do not only let the group move across apps. Let the group materialize temporary working environments for whatever it is doing now.

borrowed_ideas: agents working in the same context
changes can become part of durable state
inspirations.creative_extension: Replace the code repository and filesystem with an open-ended collaborative state containing people, ideas, relationships, decisions, questions, artifacts, events and commitments.
Use the distinction between durable state and working state for social and organisational collaboration rather than only software development.

borrowed_ideas: conversation is not automatically the artifact
questions, connections, experiments and commitments deserve different forms
the system should support returning to unfinished work
inspirations.creative_extension: A thread can generate durable traces into the wider group state without requiring the full conversation itself to become canonical knowledge.

persistent_layer.name: Collective State
persistent_layer.description: The durable substrate belonging to a person, group, community or organisation rather than an app.

collaboration_layer.name: Threads
collaboration_layer.description: The primary social rooms where people and AI work around something together.
properties: can reference other threads and objects
can change representation as the work changes

working_layer.name: Checkout
working_layer.description: A scoped working representation of the collective state relevant to the current thread or activity.

example.thread: Should we start a shared open-source AI service?

representation_layer.name: Constrained Dynamic UI
representation_layer.description: A temporary interaction surface assembled around the checkout using known interface grammars.

ai_layer.name: LLM Wings
ai_layer.description: AI capabilities embedded around human collaboration rather than positioned as the main conversational destination.
capabilities: turn discussion into structured shared state

interaction_model.default: People start by talking and working together in a thread.

evolution_example.surface: thread + experiment card + people + return point

interaction_model.important_rule: The transition between surfaces should follow collaborative intent, not application boundaries.

proposed_collaboration_world.thread: people collaborating around a question, opportunity or activity
proposed_collaboration_world.checkout: relevant slice of people, knowledge, artifacts and current state

traditional_social_media.typical_end_state: the conversation disappears down the feed

proposed_model.primary_object: collaborative thread attached to shared state
proposed_model.typical_end_state: meaningful changes become part of shared state

difference_from_saas.traditional_saas: The user enters an application's world and models their work according to its data model and interface.
difference_from_saas.proposed_model: The collective state exists independently. A suitable working surface is materialized around the current situation.
shift: from app database to shared state
from permanent UI to temporary representation
from switching apps to switching interaction grammars
from adopting software to expressing collaborative intent

key_principles: The collective persists. The interface does not have to.
The group is not a Discord server, Teams team or subreddit.
The thread is a room for doing things together, not a comment section.
The shared state belongs underneath the applications.
A checkout is the temporary working context.
The UI is a representation of the checkout, not the source of truth.
Dynamic UI should be constrained by known interaction grammars.
AI supports the humans; it is not the social centre.
Not everything said by people or generated by AI deserves to become durable state.
Important traces should survive the conversation.
The interface follows the work instead of the work following the interface.
provocations: The app is no longer the unit of software. The situation is.
What if a community could materialize whatever working environment it needs?
What if organisations maintained shared state instead of buying permanent applications for every activity?
What is the shared substrate for people collaborating, analogous to a codebase for software teams?
Social software does not have to optimise for publishing. It can optimise for doing things together.
The LLM does not need to be the room. It can give the people in the room wings.
open_questions: What exactly is the canonical unit of shared state?
How much of ATProto can be used directly and how much requires a new protocol layer?
How should private and permissioned group data work?
Can a checkout span records owned by several people or groups?
What changes are automatically durable and what requires an explicit commit-like act?
How is consent handled when AI derives new shared objects from human conversation?
How are conflicts between concurrent checkouts reconciled?
What belongs to a person versus a group versus a thread?
What are the minimum interaction primitives required for a compelling prototype?
Should the first prototype expose the checkout metaphor or keep it entirely architectural?
How does a thread transition between interaction grammars without becoming confusing?
What is the smallest real-world collaboration use case that demonstrates why this is better than Slack plus Notion plus ChatGPT?
current_best_summary: Take ATProto's portable identity, groups and typed shared data; combine it with Delta.dev's thread-plus-checkout model; replace the codebase with the evolving shared state of a human collective; and give people constrained dynamic working surfaces plus AI capabilities that help them research, think, make, decide and act together.
